acceptance: review delegate builds the packet (review-packet for the commit under review) when it is missing or was built for another commit, prints its path and size in bytes, and proceeds; review_delegate.py stays within 400 lines by putting this in review_delegate_packet.py; a test starts with no packet

The 'named in the packet but not at commit' warning skips paths git ignores (git check-ignore) and planning-sheet globs that match no file, printing one summary count instead; a test with an ignored build path asserts no warning
The packet's 'new suppressions' line numbers are the lines in the file at the commit under review; a test with a suppression added after unrelated edits pins the numbers

When review record refuses an approve over the 'not a defect because' rule, it prints each offending line (number and text) and the rule in one sentence; tests for a two-clause line and a missing-marker line

review list (rendered in review_cli.py, 387 lines, so the marking lives in review_run_status.py) and handoff status mark a failed or incomplete RUN-<model> record as superseded when a valid REVIEW-<model> was filed later at the same commit by any route, as stale-commit records are marked. Out of scope: changing the explanation rule beyond the quoted-span exception in A6

The approve rule's refusal for a line that joins two observations names the joining word and quotes both parts (the trigger is _second_observation in review_record_rules.py, which splits on ' and ' and similar conjunctions); conjunctions inside double-quoted, single-quoted or backtick spans are not split points, as code spans are already skipped; tests: a one-observation line whose ' and ' sits inside quotes or backticks is accepted, the reported shape ('not a defect because base and HEAD ...') is accepted or refused with the word and both parts named, and a line joining two independent observations with ' and ' is still refused
nodes.title: Review friction: delegate builds a missing packet, the packet skips ignored evidence and numbers suppressions correctly, refusals quote the line, and superseded failed runs say so

acceptance: edit-node accepts planned_test_changes with --set, --add and --remove like the other list fields (validated against the schema's item shape), and add-node takes --planned-test-change; a test edits it on a claimed leaf and validate passes

When integrity reports a removed or weakened test not listed in planned_test_changes, review-packet puts it under a 'Required check: unplanned test removal' heading and the reviewer prompt requires an acceptance entry for it, even with policy.integrity_gate off; an approve that omits it is refused by review record with the test name; tests for listed (no heading) and unlisted removals

docs/acceptance-evidence.md says how to authorize a test change after pickup (edit-node on the integration branch, or on the leaf branch where it is reviewed with the diff). integrity.py and roadmap_edit_fields.py stay within 400 lines (the cross-check goes in integrity_removals.py, the field handling in roadmap_edit_list_fields.py; review_packet.py, at its cap, gets the heading from review_packet_observed.py). Out of scope: turning integrity_gate on by default
nodes.title: planned_test_changes can be edited after pickup, and an unplanned test removal is a required reviewer check

acceptance: Model comparison for usage normalises case, spaces, dots and hyphens and also compares against the roster entry's harness_model and the profile's model and display names (specy_road/model_names.py), so 'Grok 4.6 High' matches a cursor-grok-4.6-high slug; a naming-only difference prints no 'model mismatch' and still estimates cost from the roster price

A real mismatch still prints the warning and leaves cost '?'; tests pin both cases with captured cursor stream-json lines. worker_adapter_parsers.py stays within 400 lines. Out of scope: reasoning-token counts the harness does not report
nodes.title: Cursor worker cost is estimated when the harness reports a display name for the rostered model

acceptance: orchestrate plan and grind-session --plan warn once per leaf when an acceptance line names a repository path (or a path's parent directory) that no touch zone covers, listing those paths; paths that do not exist and are not under any zone are listed as 'new file outside zones'; a test with one covered and one uncovered path pins the warning
The brief lists at most 20 importers per zone marked '(outside zones)' and then a count of the rest; a test with a zone of 200 importers pins the bound. Out of scope: changing zones automatically
nodes.title: Touch zones that miss what acceptance needs are flagged at plan time, and the brief's zone section stays short

acceptance: When SPECY_ROAD_REPO_ROOT names a checkout and the current directory is inside a linked worktree of the same repository, commands use the enclosing worktree and print nothing; inside a different repository they keep today's behaviour; worker delegate sets SPECY_ROAD_REPO_ROOT to the worker's worktree in its environment; a test runs ready in a linked worktree with the variable set to the main checkout

env_setup can declare symlinks (link: [node_modules, .venv]) from the main checkout into a new worktree; specy-road adds those names to the worktree's .git/info/exclude so a directory-only ignore pattern (node_modules/) does not leave them untracked, and worker delegate's clean-tree check ignores them; a test with a directory-only pattern asserts a clean status
docs/orchestration-worktrees.md says where env_setup lives and show both the command and link forms. Out of scope: copying environments
nodes.title: Linked worktrees: commands resolve the enclosing worktree, and env_setup handles symlinked environments

acceptance: decisions add --local writes the gitignored roadmap/decisions.local.yaml, which readers merge over roadmap/decisions.yaml for this clone (local wins, listed as local); decisions list shows the source; a test covers merge and precedence
pr_body_footer in roadmap/git-workflow.yaml (string, schema-checked) is appended to finish-this-task's PR body; absent means today's body

implementation_summary: commit | local in git-workflow.yaml decides whether the executor prompt says to commit work/implementation-summary-<ID>.md (commit, the default) or to leave it uncommitted for the review packet to read from the worktree (local); the prompt never tells workers to git add -f an ignored path, and with commit plus a .gitignore that ignores the file, validate says which rule wins

on_complete merge honours land: push | local for the root repository as M14.4.1 does for nested repos: local merges into the local integration branch and pushes nothing, saying so; tests for each. Out of scope: changing the defaults
nodes.title: Project preferences the workflow respects: local decisions, a PR body footer, the summary commit rule, and local landing for the root repository

acceptance: The 'Install a release candidate (TestPyPI)' section moves to docs/install-release-candidates.md; docs/install-and-usage.md keeps a two-line pointer with the same anchor text and stays within 400 lines, and every link to the old anchor (docs/upgrading.md, docs/release-runbook.md) points at the new file

The new doc shows installing an RC with an extra ([gui] as the example) for pip, pipx and uv tool from the sha256-checked wheel, and the direct-wheel-URL form ("specy-road[gui] @ https://test-files.pythonhosted.org/.../specy_road-<ver>-py3-none-any.whl") for uv tool and pipx, with how its sha256 is checked; it says that uv tool keeps a URL in its receipt, unlike a local wheel path that later disappears

It states that TestPyPI is never an index for extras or dependencies, in any form (--index-url, --extra-index-url, uv --index or --extra-index-url, any index strategy such as unsafe-best-match or first-index), because a squatted dependency name there can outrank PyPI and its setup.py runs; it names no third-party package or uploader

The extras list in install docs names every key of [project.optional-dependencies] in pyproject.toml except dev (today [gui] is missing); a test reads pyproject.toml and fails when an extra is not named in docs/install-and-usage.md or docs/install-release-candidates.md

docs/release-runbook.md A.3 step 5 (Announce the RC) says the announcement carries the filled-in pip, pipx and uv tool commands, with [gui], and the wheel's direct URL and sha256; the human publishing the release posts them. release-runbook.md stays within its 900-line override by rewording, not adding net lines. Out of scope: an rc-install-command CLI command, and changing what CI publishes
nodes.title: RC install docs cover extras and the direct wheel URL, and each RC announcement carries the filled-in command

acceptance: ci_gates in roadmap/git-workflow.yaml is schema-checked (git-workflow.schema.json has additionalProperties false, so the key is added there): a list of {name, cmd, paths}, name matching [A-Za-z0-9._-]+, cmd a non-empty string, paths an optional list of globs matched against the leaf's changed paths as touch zones are (finish_implementation_check.in_zones), no paths meaning every leaf; new specy_road/ci_gates.py reads it (git_workflow_config.py is at 396 lines and gains nothing) and refuses a duplicate name, naming it; tests for a valid list, a missing cmd (schema error) and a duplicate name

specy-road ready runs every gate whose paths match at least one path the READY records as changed (base...HEAD), from the project root as land_check_cmd runs, after the cheap refusals and after the executor's own --run commands, whether or not the executor passed any; each result is a verify row carrying gate: <name>; a non-zero exit refuses with the gate's name and output tail and never suggests --red-green; a gate skipped because no changed path matches is named in the READY body as skipped; tests with a fake failing gate, a passing gate, and a gate skipped by paths

The review packet gains a CI gates section (new specy_road/bundled_scripts/review_packet_ci_gates.py; review_packet.py, 392 lines, changes only one call line) listing every declared gate that applies to the leaf with its exit and tail from the READY when the READY commit is the commit under review, and in bold 'missing from READY' or 'not run at the commit under review' otherwise; one test per state

verify_cmd_lines (verify_cmd_config.py), which the executor brief and the reviewer prompt already carry, adds one sentence naming the leaf's applicable gates and saying a missing, stale or failing gate blocks; the project template git-workflow.yaml gains a commented ci_gates example, and new docs/git-workflow-ci-gates.md documents the key. Out of scope: running gates inside the review gate or at landing (land_check_cmd stays), auto-fix modes, per-gate timeouts, and declaring this toolkit's own gates in sr/roadmap/git-workflow.yaml (coordinator bookkeeping after landing)
nodes.title: A project declares its merge-blocking CI commands per touch zone; ready always runs them and the review packet shows their result at the reviewed commit

acceptance: run_check moves from review_gate_ready.py to new specy_road/ready_run_checks.py (review_gate_ready.py imports it); a --run that exits 0 but whose recorded tail has a line containing one of 'cannot open', 'command not found', 'No such file or directory' or 'Permission denied' (case-sensitive, one constant in that module) gets warning: '<that line>' on its verify row; ready prints the warning on stderr and still writes the READY

The review packet shows that warning in bold under the verifier's heading (review_packet.py, 392 lines, grows by at most two lines in _ready_verify); a test reproduces the reported shape (a loop whose earlier step fails with "cannot open" and whose last step succeeds, so the exit is 0) and asserts the warning in the READY and the packet, and a clean run carries none

ready --run-argv '<JSON array of strings>' (repeatable) runs that argv without a shell, records cmd as shlex.join(argv), and is otherwise a --run (same refusal on a non-zero exit, same warning); a value that is not a non-empty JSON array of strings is refused before anything runs; a test passes an argument containing $f and spaces and asserts the program receives it unexpanded. Out of scope: refusing on a marker (it is a warning), scanning beyond the recorded tail, --verify CMD=EXIT rows (they have no output), and markers beyond the four listed
nodes.title: ready does not record false evidence: a passing run whose output shows a failed command is flagged, and --run-argv runs a command without a shell

acceptance: The post-run check reads git stash list with each entry's hash and subject; new specy_road/worker_turn_stash.py parses the branch from a subject of the form 'On <branch>: <message>' or 'WIP on <branch>: <message>' for every entry added or removed during the turn; worker_turn_check.py changes only GitState's stash field and its one stash comparison

An entry on the turn's own worker's branch is a stash_rule_violation finding that quotes the subject and says the executor prompt forbids stashing, and flags that worker (post_run_findings); an entry on another worker's branch (any worker record with that branch) appends a post_run_check event with a stash_rule_violation finding to that worker's record and flags it, while this turn records an unflagged stash_other note naming that worker; each stash hash is attributed to its owner at most once, so a second observer adds no second event; an entry whose subject names no branch, or a branch no worker has, keeps today's stash finding on this worker with the subject quoted

Tests: worker A stashes and pops during worker B's turn, so A is flagged and B is not; A's own turn stashing flags A; an entry with no matching worker keeps today's finding. Out of scope: preventing the stash (the tool-call guard already denies git stash where installed) and stashes inside nested repositories
nodes.title: A change to the shared stash is attributed to the worker whose branch made it, not to whichever worker's turn ended while the entry existed

acceptance: policy.max_workers counts only live workers: states starting, running, idle and paused_by_limit (a session that can still be resumed); completed, failed and terminated records never take a slot, whatever their leaf's state (worker_orphans.holding_slots and _slot_or_existing in worker_ops_slots.py); the refusal's breakdown lists only counted workers; tests: 19 completed or failed records plus one running worker with max_workers 2 leave a slot free, and two running workers refuse

New specy_road/orphaned_claims.py lists every registry claim with no live worker (as above) on its leaf, no live session on its branch (session_presence.list_sessions), and no valid READY at its branch tip, each with its age (from the branch's last commit, else the registry row's started date) and the commands that resolve it: specy-road worker delegate <ID> to resume work, or specy-road abort-task-pickup to release it; handoff status prints the list (review_cli.py, 400 lines, does not grow: an existing line is folded) and doctor prints it as a report-only section that --fix never acts on; tests: a claim with a failed worker and no READY is listed, and claims with a running worker, a live session or a READY at the tip are not

When worker delegate fails after the leaf is claimed (a slot refusal, a usage limit, a launch error), its error ends with '<ID> stays claimed with no worker: retry `specy-road worker delegate <ID>` or release it with `specy-road abort-task-pickup`' (worker_cli.py, 397 lines, changes one existing line); grind-session's hook_failed line for phase implement (grind_session_events.py, today 'phase=implement node=<ID> rc=<n>') adds that the leaf stays claimed and the same two commands, pinned by a test; the orchestrate command's delegate step (specyrd-orchestrate.md) says to resolve such a claim before the next pickup. Out of scope: rolling back the claim or removing the worktree automatically, and claims held by another clone (doctor's registry section covers rows with no branch)
nodes.title: A claim left with no worker is never silent: finished workers free their max_workers slot, handoff status and doctor list orphaned claims, and a failed delegate says how to resolve its claim

acceptance: A sanitized fixture under tests/fixtures/ holds a multi-segment Cursor stream-json turn (only type, subtype, session_id and usage fields kept; no prompt or content text), taken from a real long turn's worker log; the implementation summary states which line types carry usage and whether each count is per segment or a running total, as observed in that fixture

The cursor adapter counts every usage-bearing line of a turn: per-segment counts are summed and a running total is taken once at its last value, so the turn's usage, as worker usage sums it, equals the turn's real total; a test with the fixture asserts output_tokens equal the sum of the segments, and a single-result short turn keeps today's numbers

worker usage (and --json, as possible_undercount: true) marks a turn as 'possible undercount' when it lasted 20 minutes or more (from its start event to its usage event) and reported fewer than 300 output tokens per minute, both constants in new specy_road/worker_usage_plausibility.py; tests: the reported shape (6,092 s, 10,136 output tokens) is marked and a 5-minute turn with 17,000 is not. Out of scope: other harnesses' parsers, diff size as a signal, and correcting the recorded cost
nodes.title: worker usage counts every usage-bearing event of a long Cursor turn and marks a turn whose output tokens are implausibly low for its length

acceptance: rework_lines and rework_check apply review list's staleness rule (same_commit with the branch tip): blocks at the tip are listed as today; blocks at an earlier commit follow under '### Earlier blocks (possibly resolved)', each with its commit and required changes and one sentence telling the executor to confirm each is addressed by a later commit and say so in the implementation summary; the stderr note reads 'carries N blocking review(s) at the tip and M earlier (possibly resolved)'; earlier blocks alone still count as something to rework from

worker delegate --rework --note <file> copies the file to work/reviews/<NODE_ID>/REWORK-NOTE.md stamped with the branch tip's sha; the ## Rework section carries it under '### Coordinator directive', after the accepted RCA when one is carried and before the reviews, only while the branch tip is that sha, so a note never reaches a later rework after a new commit; --note without --rework, or a missing or empty file, is refused before any launch; --op-id binds the note's text, not its path

worker_cli.py (397 lines) does not grow: delegate's parser and cmd_delegate move to new specy_road/bundled_scripts/worker_cli_delegate.py. Tests: the reported case (one block at an earlier commit fixed by a later commit, one block at the tip) lists one tip block and one possibly-resolved block; a note appears above the reviews and is dropped after a new commit; a leaf with only tip blocks and no note gets today's prompt byte for byte. Out of scope: deciding whether a later commit resolved an earlier block (the reviewer does) and RCA carrying (M15.6)
nodes.title: --rework carries blocks at the branch tip as required changes, lists older blocks as possibly resolved, and takes a coordinator note placed above the reviews

acceptance: specy-road prompt --role reviewer with --channel paste or --channel subagent writes RUN-<model>.json at the commit under review with state started and source prompt-paste or prompt-subagent (reviewer_run_failure.py gains the writer beside open_reviewer_cli_run; role_prompt.py changes only its call line), and prints on stderr that a reviewer stopped by a rate or usage limit should be re-dispatched or waited out, since specy-road does not retry these channels

New specy-road review start <NODE_ID> --model <id> writes the same marker (source review-start) for a reviewer launched any other way, refusing a model that is not a roster reviewer; its parser lives in new specy_road/bundled_scripts/review_cli_start.py, and review_cli.py (400 lines) does not grow

review list and handoff status show a started RUN with no REVIEW-<model> at the same commit as 'started <age> ago, not filed', and as superseded once a REVIEW-<model> is filed at that commit by any route (review_run_status.py, from M15.17); tests: a paste-channel marker with no record, the same after a record is filed, and a review start marker. Out of scope: retrying subagent or paste runs, detecting the limit itself, and changing review delegate's capacity retry
nodes.title: A review that stops before filing leaves a trace: every reviewer channel opens a RUN record, and review list shows started but not filed

acceptance: policy.full_leaf_checklist (boolean, default false) is schema-checked in orchestration.yaml; when true, the review gate at a commit needs, among its counting approvals, at least one full review (no delta_from) whose record carries full_leaf_checklist with ci_gates, dropped_text and test_diff each pass or n/a, and otherwise reports 'no full-leaf checklist approval at this commit'; the rule lives in new specy_road/review_gate_checklist.py and review_gate.py (398 lines) changes only one call line; review-record.schema.json (additionalProperties false) gains the optional key

The full packet gains a Full-leaf checklist section (new specy_road/bundled_scripts/review_packet_checklist.py; review_packet.py changes only one call line): CI gates points at the CI gates section (M15.23) for this commit; dropped text lists lines removed in merge-base...commit, outside Markdown files, that are comments (#, // or /* after indentation) or contain a quoted string, at most 50 with a count of the rest; test diff lists the test files changed and the integrity report's removed or renamed tests; a delta packet carries one line saying another reviewer must file the checklist this round when no checklist approval is on file

New docs/orchestration-full-leaf-checklist.md documents the policy and the record key. Tests: a delta approval plus a full approval with a passing checklist meets the gate; two delta approvals do not, with the message; a checklist with a fail item does not count; with the policy off the gate is unchanged. Out of scope: choosing which reviewer files the checklist (the coordinator does), and changing delta_review's qualifying rules
nodes.title: Under delta review, one approval per round still checks the whole leaf against the merge base on a fixed checklist
